facts.label: Evidence, risk mechanism and consequence
facts.text: First, the debt: S4 page:19 gives the maturity table by facility, "Total $ 897,750 $ 20,000 $ 61,043 $ 978,793", which is a filed statement and fully supports the facility-level debt and maturity-wall work; the risk is only that the instrument terms behind it (guarantees, security, covenant levels) are not in the pack, so CP-2 must describe those as stated by the registrant and not test them. Second, liquidity: S4 page:32 states "$479.2 million of unused commitments under the Credit Agreement" and S4 page:17 gives letters of credit and interest rates, so liquidity can be built from filed inputs; the amount of any facility expiring within twelve months is answerable from the maturity dates in S4 page:18 (revolver 2030-05-02, term loan 2033-05-05). Third, earnings quality: the Q3 results are the first full quarter with the acquired business, so Q3 2026 is not a run-rate-comparable quarter to any 2025 quarter; the only acquisition-adjusted earnings measure is a management figure with no schedule (S7 page:5 "does not reflect all adjustments that would otherwise be required in connection with the preparation of pro forma financial statements"), so CP-1 and CP-2 must label it as management-attributed and not use it as audited or pro forma. Fourth, contingent items: the earn-out to the seller carries a maximum of USD 125.0 million payable in cash or equity at the Company's option (S4 page:10), and the Fleet sale earn-out receivable of up to USD 65.0 million was carried at nil after a USD 29.2 million fair value write-down in 2025, and its preliminary results show the threshold was not achieved (S4 page:25 "the earn-out performance threshold was not achieved"); both are note disclosures consumers must carry.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot, and it describes a business that changed shape during 2026. Revenue and earnings are strong and the filed statements are complete for every period needed, but the perimeter now includes the Precision Aviation Group business acquired on 2026-05-05, which contributed USD 173.7 million of the USD 541.0 million of Q3 2026 revenue, so FY2025 and Q3 2026 are not like-for-like. The acquisition took debt from USD 296.3 million to USD 978.8 million of principal while about USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the cash price (S4 page:29); net debt over management's trailing adjusted EBITDA is 3.04x, or 2.35x if management's pre-acquisition earnings are accepted, against 1.24x at the end of 2025. Liquidity is adequate, and the debt is mostly secured floating-rate bank debt maturing in 2030 and 2033. The weak points are cash conversion (nine-month free cash flow negative after a large inventory build), a quarter with a non-cash earn-out gain inside operating income, add-backs of about a tenth of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, and the absence of covenant levels. Those points limit confidence in leverage trajectory and headroom, not in the reported balance sheet.

facts.label: Reconciliations and quality of earnings
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure. For 9M 2026 it adds 27,084 to EBITDA of 221,535 to reach 248,619 (S7 page:7): acquisition, integration and restructuring costs 18,431, stock-based compensation 12,992, a loss on debt extinguishment 4,473 and divestiture-related costs 68, less an earn-out fair value gain of 8,880. The add-backs are about 10.9% of Adjusted EBITDA. In Q3 2026 the earn-out gain of 8,880 is deducted in the bridge from EBITDA of 107,581 to Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165, together with 4,059 of acquisition costs and 4,405 of stock compensation (S7 page:7), but it remains inside reported operating income of 77,451 and net income of 47,264. Q3 2025 shows the opposite: a 23,300 earn-out charge depressed reported operating income of 10,087 (S4 page:4). Comparing Q3 2026 with Q3 2025 reported earnings therefore overstates the underlying change; Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165 against 47,351 is the cleaner comparison but is still a management figure and still mixes perimeters (PAG contributed 173,666 of Q3 2026 revenue, S4 page:30). The retained quarters tie: Q1 55,430 plus Q2 86,024 equals H1 2026 of 141,454 (S6 page:7), and H1 plus Q3 107,165 equals the 9M 2026 figure of 248,619.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: VSE is a single-segment aviation aftermarket business that sells parts (distribution) and repairs components and engines (repair), and in 2026 it bought its way into a larger engine-repair and distribution platform. The strongest support for a creditor is that the largest deal, Precision Aviation Group (PAG), was funded with a large equity raise and tangible equity units alongside a USD 900.0 million term loan B, that PAG already contributes about a third of quarterly revenue, and that the group has raised equity repeatedly since 2024 to fund acquisitions. The weakest points are concentration (one affiliated customer group at about 20% of FY2025 revenue), dependence on OEM licenses and approvals for the highest-value repairs, and an acquisition pace that leaves purchase accounting preliminary for several deals at once. What decides the outcome is integration of PAG and the Q4 2026 cash flow, because debt now rests mostly on floating-rate bank facilities, and because the documents that govern control rights (credit agreement, purchase agreement amendment, exchange and registration agreements) are not in the pack. Management's characterisations (record results, leading position, sole-source repairs) are quoted as Management Language below and are not adopted.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction that defines the period is the acquisition of Precision Aviation Group (PAG), a portfolio company of GenNx360 Capital Partners, under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2026-01-29 and completed on 2026-05-05. Status: completed. The parties named in the executed agreement listing are VSE Corporation, two VSE acquisition vehicles, GenNx/PAG IntermediateCo Inc. and GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC (S1 page:79); a first amendment to the agreement dated 2026-05-04, an exchange and redemption agreement, a registration rights agreement and two lock-up agreements, all dated 2026-05-05 and all with GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC, are listed as exhibits (S3 page:33), but none of those documents is in the pack, so their terms are Insufficient Information. The second-quarter 10-Q summarises the deal as total consideration of "approximately $2.02 billion" (S3 page:9). The 10-K and the first-quarter 10-Q describe total upfront consideration of approximately USD 2.025 billion, in the Q1 10-Q "consisting of $1.750 billion in cash" plus an in-kind payment of 1,415,752 shares of newly issued equity of a VSE subsidiary, with up to USD 125.0 million of contingent earn-out on PAG's 2026 adjusted EBITDA (S1 page:73; S2 page:20). The later 10-Qs record total purchase consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand: cash paid 1,770,370, less cash acquired 22,215, equity at fair value 238,002 and an earn-out at acquisition-date fair value of 33,850 (S3 page:9; S4 page:9 and page:10). These are two bases for the same deal and are logged as a conflict below, not reconciled.

The later 10-Qs record total purchase consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand: cash paid 1,770,370, less cash acquired 22,215, equity at fair value 238,002 and an earn-out at acquisition-date fair value of 33,850 (S3 page:9; S4 page:9 and page:10). These are two bases for the same deal and are logged as a conflict below, not reconciled.

facts.text: Use of proceeds and sources. The cash price was funded by a February 2026 common stock offering of 4,587,766 shares at USD 188.00 per share (net proceeds USD 829.0 million) and a tangible equity unit offering of 9,200,000 units at a stated USD 50.00 each (net proceeds USD 444.9 million), together about USD 1.3 billion net, plus borrowings of USD 900.0 million under a new term loan B (S4 page:26 and page:29; S2 page:20). Each unit combines a prepaid stock purchase contract, settled in shares on 2029-02-01 within a range of 0.2171 to 0.2660 shares per contract, and a senior unsecured amortizing note paying 5.93% per annum with final installment on 2029-02-01 (S4 page:19, page:26 and page:27). Liquidity effect and leverage after the deal are in the prior handoff (CP-1): principal debt of USD 978.8 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 296.3 million at 2025-12-31.

rows.label: VSE is a listed aviation aftermarket distributor and repairer that changed shape in 2026 through the PAG purchase, funded mainly by equity and a new term loan. Customer concentration, OEM dependence and integration are the business risks.
The PAG acquisition closed on 2026-05-05 at about USD 2.02 billion of accounting consideration and repair rose to 58.8% of Q3 2026 revenue from 37.8% a year earlier.
Funding was mainly equity, about USD 1.3 billion net of offering proceeds, plus a USD 900.0 million term loan B; no sponsor or controlling holder is named.
About one fifth of FY2025 revenue came from one affiliated customer group, and engine repair rests on OEM licenses and repair approvals.
The PAG seller holds exchangeable shares under lock-up and registration rights, and an earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million may be paid in cash or equity at VSE's option.
The PAG headline price of USD 2.025 billion and the accounting consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand differ, and the sources give no bridge.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: VSE Corporation is a profitable aviation aftermarket credit that has become much larger and materially more leveraged, and its credit quality now depends on integrating the Precision Aviation Group business and turning earnings into cash. The strongest support is earnings growth, with a record Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.8% in Q3 2026, liquidity of USD 545.0 million and annual scheduled principal of no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031. The weakest point is cash conversion: free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million for the nine months to September 2026 while net debt stands at 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA and the covenant levels are unknown. Delivery of the fourth-quarter cash flow management expects, with margins holding, decides the outcome.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. VSE has levered up through an equity-heavy acquisition, and its leverage path is mostly a matter of earnings timing. Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA against 1.24x at December 2025 [CP-1 leverage chart; S7 page:7], because the trailing earnings include only five months of the acquired business while all of its debt is on the balance sheet. Management's full-year 2026 guidance of revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.9% to 19.1% [S7 page:3] implies full-year Adjusted EBITDA of about USD 347 million to USD 354 million (calculated below), which would put net debt at about 2.6x on a flat net debt. This is a mechanical, not a proven, deleveraging, and it relies on guidance that the filings do not yet evidence (Analyst Interpretation on a Management Language basis). The credit implication is that leverage tolerance is acceptable if the guided run-rate is delivered and thin if the acquired earnings disappoint.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 2. VSE's liquidity and maturity profile make near-term default or refinancing risk low. Cash of USD 65.8 million and unused revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million total USD 545.0 million against USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months, and annual scheduled principal is no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031, with the balance of the term loan due from 2032, mostly at its 2033 maturity [CP-1 maturity wall; S4 page:19]. The risk mechanic that remains is acquisition spending: the revolver helps fund bolt-on deals (Atech, acquired on 2026-08-31, was funded with cash and revolver borrowings, and USD 20.0 million was drawn at 2026-09-30 [S4 page:9 and page:17]) so liquidity can fall if acquisitions continue before free cash flow turns up.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 3. Cash conversion is the weak spot. Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months and free cash flow negative USD 3.4 million, after a USD 148.4 million inventory build [CP-1; S4 page:6], while Q3 2026 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million. Growth programs, including the new OEM auxiliary power unit program the Company names [S4 page:33], absorb inventory ahead of revenue. The credit implication is that debt reduction comes from year-end working capital release and earnings, not from structural cash generation shown so far; the write-down of slow-moving inventories was a critical audit matter in FY2025 [S1 page:40].

Secured floating debt is USD 917.75 million with USD 250.0 million of swaps, leaving about USD 667.8 million exposed; each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest, about 2.2% of trailing adjusted EBITDA (calculated below). rows.label: VSE is a profitable but newly stretched aviation aftermarket credit: net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA after a large acquisition, liquidity is adequate, and the outcome hinges on integration and year-end cash flow.
Net debt rose to 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA from 1.24x at December 2025; management guidance implies about 2.6x at year-end even if net debt does not fall.
Liquidity of USD 545.0 million covers the USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months many times; the revolver matures in 2030 and the term loan in 2033.
Free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million for nine months after a large inventory build, though the third quarter produced USD 46.6 million.
About USD 667.8 million of floating-rate secured debt is unhedged, so each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest.
One customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue, OEM licenses support repair margins, and goodwill and intangibles are 62.6% of assets.

This handoff assesses source readiness for VSE CORP (registrant VSE Corporation, ticker VSEC, Delaware; issuer id vsec) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025. The cutoff is 2026-11-05. The requested downstream work is CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. This module answers one question: can the seven supplied filed sources support that work, and what stays blocked. It gives no credit conclusion and calculates no credit metric. The context file holds the run settings only, and its blank fields (ratings, quotes, deal terms, peers, research questions) are left blank, not read as zero.
## Sources

How far each source was read: S4 and S7 were read in full (36 of 36 and 13 of 13 pages). S1, S2, S3, S5 and S6 were searched for debt, liquidity, covenant, acquisition, subsequent-event, definition and cash-flow content and read at the pages cited below; their remaining pages (S1 business, risk factors, tax, equity compensation and exhibit pages in particular) were located by heading but not read line by line. That is a bounded inspection, not a full fidelity review of those five sources.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed sources support financial, business and credit work on VSE through the third quarter of 2026, with limitations. They do not support covenant headroom or guarantor analysis, because the credit agreement and its amendment are absent. | Medium | Covenant levels, guarantor list and the amended credit agreement are not supplied; acquisition-adjusted earnings cannot be rebuilt from the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt by facility, maturities, liquidity and interest rates are disclosed at the latest quarter end in the filed quarterly report. | Facility-level debt, maturity and liquidity work can proceed from filed statements. | High |

| The filings say a maximum net leverage test and a minimum interest coverage test exist and were met, but give no levels or step-downs. | Covenant headroom cannot be measured until the credit agreement and its amendment are supplied. | High |

| The May 2026 acquisition added a large new business, and its purchase accounting is still preliminary. | Comparisons with 2025 mix different perimeters; trend and leverage work needs pro forma care. | High |

| Management leverage ratios use net debt after issuance costs and, for the lower ratio, earnings including pre-acquisition periods with no component schedule. | Reported leverage is a management measure, not covenant leverage, and part of it cannot be verified. | Medium |

| Cash paid for interest and taxes appears only in the annual report; the 2026 interim reports do not give it. | Cash interest cover for 2026 cannot be built from cash paid; only expense figures are available. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested work. Every period the run needs is covered by a filed statement: FY2025 audited (S1) and Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 unaudited (S2, S3, S4), each with balance sheet, operations, cash flow and notes, plus three earnings releases (S5, S6, S7) that supply discrete quarters, non-GAAP reconciliations, net debt and leverage tables, and guidance. The strongest contrary evidence is that the legal documents behind the debt are absent: the registrant states a maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio but never prints a level, and the May 2026 amendment that created the USD 900.0 million term loan B is described only in the notes. That does not stop the financial, business or credit work, but it blocks covenant headroom, guarantor and security analysis and any claim about definitions in the credit agreement. The second limitation is perimeter: the Precision Aviation Group acquisition on 2026-05-05 contributed USD 173.7 million of Q3 2026 revenue of USD 541.0 million (S4 page:29 and page:30), so FY2025 and the first four months of 2026 describe a different business from Q3 2026, and the acquisition accounting is preliminary. The next evidence action is to obtain the credit agreement dated 2025-05-02, the first amendment dated 2026-05-05, and the amortizing-note terms, and to have each consumer use filed statements ahead of release figures wherever the two differ.
### Source assessment
| Label | Original authority and perimeter | Period and basis | Located evidence | Limitation carried forward |

| S1 | Filed audited annual report of VSE Corporation, consolidated, with the auditor's opinion | FY2025, year ended 2025-12-31, USD thousands, continuing operations after the Federal and Defense and Fleet sales | S1 page:39 "present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2025 and 2024" | Pre-dates the 2026 acquisition and the new term loan B; describes the PAG deal as a subsequent event (S1 page:73) |

| S2 | Filed unaudited interim report, consolidated | Q1 2026, quarter ended 2026-03-31 | S2 page:4 "Cash and cash equivalents $ 1,239,407 $ 69,358" | Cash of that size is pre-closing; the acquisition and new facilities are subsequent events at this date |

| S3 | Filed unaudited interim report, consolidated | Q2 2026 and six months to 2026-06-30 | S3 page:15 "Principal amount of long-term debt 966,668 296,250" | First balance sheet after the acquisition; purchase accounting preliminary |

| S4 | Filed unaudited interim report, consolidated; latest filed statements | Q3 2026 and nine months to 2026-09-30 | S4 page:17 "Principal amount of long-term debt 978,793 296,250" | Signed 2026-11-05, the cutoff date (S4 page:36 "Date: November 5, 2026 By: /s/ John A. Cuomo"); purchase accounting preliminary |

| S5 | Management earnings release, furnished, not a filed statement | Q1 2026, with non-GAAP measures | S5 page:6 "Net Debt $ (878,432) $ 223,446" | Non-GAAP definitions differ from later releases; supporting claims only |
| S6 | Management earnings release | Q2 2026 and six months | S6 page:8 "Net Debt $ 871,597 $ 223,446" | Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS definition changed; supporting claims only |

| S7 | Management earnings release | Q3 2026 and nine months | S7 page:7 "TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations (2) $ 389,234 $ 209,128" | Latest management measures and guidance; supporting claims only; the accompanying call materials are not in the pack |

Entity and perimeter. All seven sources report VSE Corporation consolidated (single reportable segment, Aviation: S4 page:21 "manages its business as a single reportable and operating segment"). No parent, sponsor or stand-alone borrower statements exist; the context names no borrower, parent or guarantors. The borrower under the credit agreement is the Company, with subsidiary guarantors, per the exhibit list (S1 page:81 "10.8 Credit Agreement, dated as of May 2, 2025"), but no source names the guarantors, so the restricted or guaranteeing group is an unresolved distinction. The seller of the acquired target was paid partly in newly issued equity of an unnamed VSE subsidiary (S4 page:10, 1,415,752 shares, exchangeable one-for-one into Company common stock by 2029-05-05); that subsidiary is not identified.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand met | What is carried forward |

| CP-1 financial base | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual and interim statements, discrete quarter data in releases, debt by facility in S4 page:17 and page:19, segment and revenue-type tables in S4 page:16 and page:17 | Perimeter break at 2026-05-05; Q4 2025 is not reported alone; no 2026 cash-paid interest or taxes; reconciliation of non-GAAP figures not performed here |

| CP-1A business and transaction | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Acquisition notes for PAG, Atech, NorthStar, Aero 3 in S4 page:8 to page:15; financing offerings in S4 page:25 to page:27 | Preliminary purchase accounting; no executed purchase agreement, no pro forma EBITDA; Test Logic price not disclosed |

| CP-2 credit | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Debt by facility, maturity table, liquidity, swaps, compliance statement | Covenant levels, definitions, margins on the amended facilities and guarantor structure not supplied; no ratings or market quotes in context |
| CP-5 evidence trace | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | All seven sources are locatable by page | Must carry every gap below and the release-versus-filing precedence rule |
### Conflicts and version relationships

The three 10-Qs and the 10-K are successive periods, not versions of one another; each stays an active source. The three releases are management documents and each stays active. Where a release and a filing differ, the filing controls and the release is an attributed claim. The differences found are listed here with locators and their effect.
| Item | Source A | Source B | Effect downstream |

| PAG consideration | S2 page:20 "total upfront consideration of approximately $2.025 billion, consisting of $1.750 billion in cash" | S4 page:10 "Total purchase consideration $ 2,020,007" (thousands; cash paid 1,770,370, equity 238,002 and earn-out fair value 33,850, from S4 page:9 and page:10) | Different bases (headline upfront versus accounting consideration at fair value, with working-capital adjustments); not reconciled here. CP-1A must quote each with its basis |

| Revolver availability at 2026-06-30 | S6 page:3 "approximately $500.0 million available under its revolving credit facility" | S3 page:29 "$499.3 million of unused commitments under the Credit Agreement" | Release rounds; use the filing figure for liquidity |

| Term loan naming | S1 page:74 refers to a "New Term Loan A Facility" upsize under the debt commitment letter | S4 page:18 describes a new "senior secured term loan B facility" that "replaced the Company's previous term loan"; S5 page:2 "The new Term Loan B refinanced and replaced the Company's existing Term Loan A." | The commitment-stage structure in the 10-K was superseded by the executed structure; use S4 for the structure |

| Adjusted measures | S5 page:4 "Adjusted EBITDA margin represents estimated operating income before depreciation and amortization expenses as a percentage of revenue", and Adjusted Net Income there is adjusted only for acquisition-related costs and other discrete items | S6 page:1 "which reflect a change in the definition of Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS (Diluted)"; S7 page:4 "Beginning with the second quarter of 2026, Adjusted Net Income from continuing operations and Adjusted EPS" | Q1 adjusted net income and EPS in S5 are not comparable with Q2 and Q3 figures; prior periods are restated retrospectively in S6 and S7 only |

| Leverage measures | S7 page:5 "differ from the Total Net Leverage Ratio as defined in the Company" (credit agreement) | S4 page:19 covenant is a "maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio" with no level | Reported net leverage ratios cannot be used as covenant headroom |

Net debt as the releases define it deducts debt issuance costs as well as cash (S7 page:5 "Net debt is defined as principal amount of debt less debt issuance costs and less cash and cash equivalents"). That is a management definition and differs from principal less cash; consumers must state which they use.
### Evidence, risk mechanism and consequence

First, the debt: S4 page:19 gives the maturity table by facility, "Total $ 897,750 $ 20,000 $ 61,043 $ 978,793", which is a filed statement and fully supports the facility-level debt and maturity-wall work; the risk is only that the instrument terms behind it (guarantees, security, covenant levels) are not in the pack, so CP-2 must describe those as stated by the registrant and not test them. Second, liquidity: S4 page:32 states "$479.2 million of unused commitments under the Credit Agreement" and S4 page:17 gives letters of credit and interest rates, so liquidity can be built from filed inputs; the amount of any facility expiring within twelve months is answerable from the maturity dates in S4 page:18 (revolver 2030-05-02, term loan 2033-05-05). Third, earnings quality: the Q3 results are the first full quarter with the acquired business, so Q3 2026 is not a run-rate-comparable quarter to any 2025 quarter; the only acquisition-adjusted earnings measure is a management figure with no schedule (S7 page:5 "does not reflect all adjustments that would otherwise be required in connection with the preparation of pro forma financial statements"), so CP-1 and CP-2 must label it as management-attributed and not use it as audited or pro forma. Fourth, contingent items: the earn-out to the seller carries a maximum of USD 125.0 million payable in cash or equity at the Company's option (S4 page:10), and the Fleet sale earn-out receivable of up to USD 65.0 million was carried at nil after a USD 29.2 million fair value write-down in 2025, and its preliminary results show the threshold was not achieved (S4 page:25 "the earn-out performance threshold was not achieved"); both are note disclosures consumers must carry.
## Calculations
No credit metric, ratio, reconciliation or normalization is calculated in this handoff, as the method requires. Coverage counts only:
| Item | Inputs | Result |
| Pages in the seven sources | 82 + 28 + 34 + 36 + 10 + 13 + 13 | 216 pages |
| Sources read in full | S4 36 of 36 pages; S7 13 of 13 pages | 2 of 7 sources |
| Sources searched and read at cited pages | S1, S2, S3, S5, S6 | 5 of 7 sources |
| Sources with blocked preparation | None; all 7 converted to text with extractable content | 0 of 7 |
## Gaps

- Credit agreement and first amendment: Not supplied. The pack holds no legal document (context attachment field `legal_documents` is none). The credit agreement of 2025-05-02 appears only as an exhibit list entry (S1 page:81) and the first amendment of 2026-05-05 only in the notes (S4 page:18); the 10-Q exhibit list (S4 page:36) carries only certifications and XBRL files. Missing: covenant levels and step-downs, definitions of Total Net Leverage Ratio and Interest Coverage Ratio, post-amendment margin grid, commitment fee, security package, guarantor names, dividend limit amount, mandatory prepayment terms. Searched for "maximum Total Net", "not exceed", "Interest Coverage" and "guarantor" across all seven sources; only the generic statement at S4 page:19 was found. Affects CP-2 (covenants), CP-1A (structure). Remediation: supply both documents.

- Amortizing notes terms: the notes' interest rate (5.93 percent), installments and final date (2029-02-01) are in S4 page:19, but no indenture or supplemental indenture is supplied; ranking is described only as "senior unsecured amortizing notes".

- Cash paid for interest and income taxes in 2026: Not supplied. Searched "interest paid", "cash paid for interest", "paid for interest", "income taxes paid" and "taxes paid" in all seven sources. Only S1 page:44 has them ("Cash paid for interest $ 26,849 $ 37,076 $ 35,039"), for FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023. The interim supplemental disclosure (S4 page:7) lists only non-cash items. Affects CP-1 and CP-2.

- Q4 2025 discrete quarter: not reported alone in any source. S1 gives FY2025; S4 and S7 give the nine months to 2025-09-30. Any Q4 figure would be derived downstream. The nine-month 2025 comparatives in S4 carry reclassifications (S4 page:8 "Certain reclassifications have been made to the prior year consolidated financial statements"), so a derived Q4 needs a perimeter check.

- Cash flow perimeter in 2025 comparatives: the cash flow statement combines continuing and discontinued operations (S7 page:12 "The cash flows related to discontinued operations and held-for-sale assets and liabilities have not been segregated"); free cash flow comparatives for 2025 therefore include the Fleet business.

- Acquisition-adjusted earnings: the TTM Acquisition Adjusted EBITDA (S7 page:7) includes pre-acquisition earnings with no component schedule; the only pro forma figures in the filing are revenue and net income from continuing operations (S4 page:11), not EBITDA. Not calculable from the pack: pre-acquisition EBITDA of the acquired businesses.

- Purchase accounting: the allocation for PAG, Atech, NorthStar, Aero 3 and the PT6 fuel pump license is preliminary (S4 page:8 to page:15). The Test Logic acquisition on 2026-10-05 is a subsequent event with no price disclosed (S4 page:27).

- Customer concentration after the acquisition: S1 page:11 states a group of affiliated customers was "approximately 20% of the Company" revenue for FY2025; the 2026 interim reports contain no updated concentration disclosure (searched "customer group" and "concentration" in S2, S3, S4).

- Entity identity: guarantors, restricted group and the VSE subsidiary that issued the exchangeable shares are unnamed (see Sources). Hierarchy of claims across the parent and subsidiaries cannot be mapped.
- Ratings, market prices, yield, peer and precedent data: Not supplied (context lists none); outside this pack.

- Call materials: the Q3 release says presentation materials will accompany the 2026-11-05 call (S7 page:8 "accompanying presentation materials will be available"); no presentation or transcript is in the pack, and no slide or chart coverage is claimed. The three releases stand in for presentations.

- Extraction fidelity: all sources are text conversions of HTML. Tables are flattened into lines and footnote markers sit inline; no fidelity review against the original filing or the inline XBRL (listed in S4 page:36) has been done. Consumers should confirm any figure they depend on against the quoted row.

- Dates: the Q3 10-Q is signed on the cutoff date, so nothing in the pack is later than the cutoff; the 2026-11-05 call is an event on the cutoff date and its content is not in the pack. Future dates in the sources (maturities, settlement, earn-out period) are contract terms, not events.

- Currency and period: all figures are USD, in thousands in the statements and in millions in narrative; no foreign-currency reporting basis differs from the context (the foreign currency translation line in S4 page:5 is a small other-comprehensive-income item). Periods match the context: current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025.

This handoff builds the financial base for VSE CORP (registrant VSE Corporation, ticker VSEC, issuer id vsec) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, cutoff 2026-11-05. It extracts the reported statements, debt by instrument, liquidity, covenant disclosure, claims outside debt, the latest quarter and subsequent events, then calculates leverage, liquidity and cover on stated bases. Amounts are USD; statement figures are in thousands (USD k) and the chart tables are in US$m or x as their headings require. All figures come from the seven pinned sources below. No outside knowledge of the company is used.

It was opened and used: its status (READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS), the perimeter break at 2026-05-05, the missing credit agreement and first amendment, the missing 2026 cash interest, and the rule that filed statements control over release figures are all carried below. S1 to S4 are filed statements and control; S5 to S7 are management releases and are cited as attributed figures. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| VSE's financial base is usable but newly leveraged: debt rose to USD 978.8 million after the May 2026 acquisition, giving 3.26x debt to trailing EBITDA, while free cash flow this year is thin and covenant headroom cannot be measured. | Medium | Covenant levels, amended-facility margins and 2026 cash interest are not in the pack, and acquisition-adjusted earnings are a management figure with no schedule. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA at September 2026, against 1.24x at December 2025, because the acquisition was financed with debt and equity. | Leverage is far higher than at December 2025; reduction depends on earnings growth and free cash flow rather than scheduled repayment. | Medium |

| Of the debt, 93.8 percent is secured bank debt at floating rates; the unsecured amortizing notes are the remainder. | Secured lenders rank ahead of the notes, and only part of the floating exposure is hedged by swaps. | High |

| Free cash flow was negative for the nine months to September 2026, with a positive third quarter; an inventory build absorbed cash. | Debt reduction this year leans on a strong fourth quarter that management expects but the filings do not yet show. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 479.2 million of unused revolver commitments plus USD 65.8 million of cash, and scheduled repayments before 2030 are small. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; the maturity wall sits in 2033 with the term loan. | High |

| The only cash interest figure is for FY2025; 2026 interest cover must rest on expense and contractual-rate estimates. | Coverage for 2026 is an estimate, not a cash measure, until cash interest is disclosed. | High |
### Financial base view

The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot, and it describes a business that changed shape during 2026. Revenue and earnings are strong and the filed statements are complete for every period needed, but the perimeter now includes the Precision Aviation Group business acquired on 2026-05-05, which contributed USD 173.7 million of the USD 541.0 million of Q3 2026 revenue, so FY2025 and Q3 2026 are not like-for-like. The acquisition took debt from USD 296.3 million to USD 978.8 million of principal while about USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the cash price (S4 page:29); net debt over management's trailing adjusted EBITDA is 3.04x, or 2.35x if management's pre-acquisition earnings are accepted, against 1.24x at the end of 2025. Liquidity is adequate, and the debt is mostly secured floating-rate bank debt maturing in 2030 and 2033. The weak points are cash conversion (nine-month free cash flow negative after a large inventory build), a quarter with a non-cash earn-out gain inside operating income, add-backs of about a tenth of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, and the absence of covenant levels. Those points limit confidence in leverage trajectory and headroom, not in the reported balance sheet.
### Reporting entity and perimeter

The reporting entity is VSE Corporation consolidated (S4 page:21, single reportable segment, Aviation); there is no stand-alone borrower, parent or sponsor statement, and the context names none. The borrower under the credit agreement is the Company, with subsidiary guarantors named only generically in the exhibit list (S1 page:81 "each subsidiary of the Company from time to time party thereto as guarantors"). Amounts are continuing operations unless marked. The cash flow statement still combines continuing and discontinued operations for 2025 comparatives (S7 page:12 "The cash flows related to discontinued operations and held-for-sale assets and liabilities have not been segregated"), so 2025 operating cash flow and free cash flow include the Fleet business until its April 2025 sale. Periods used: FY2025, Q1 to Q3 2026 and Q3 2025, nine months (9M) 2025 and 2026, and trailing twelve months (TTM) as management prints them.

No facility expires within twelve months; scheduled principal due within twelve months is the current portion of long-term debt, USD 32.344 million (S4 page:4). ### Liquidity

The revolver matures 2030-05-02, so none of it expires within twelve months. The prior quarter-ends were USD 69.4 million cash and USD 399.4 million unused at 2025-12-31 (S1 page:33 and page:41), USD 1,239.4 million and USD 399.3 million at 2026-03-31 (S2 page:4 and page:23), and USD 75.4 million and USD 499.3 million at 2026-06-30 (S3 page:4 and page:29). The 2026-03-31 cash was offering proceeds held for the 2026-05-05 closing and is not an operating liquidity level. ### Reconciliations and quality of earnings

Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure. For 9M 2026 it adds 27,084 to EBITDA of 221,535 to reach 248,619 (S7 page:7): acquisition, integration and restructuring costs 18,431, stock-based compensation 12,992, a loss on debt extinguishment 4,473 and divestiture-related costs 68, less an earn-out fair value gain of 8,880. The add-backs are about 10.9% of Adjusted EBITDA. In Q3 2026 the earn-out gain of 8,880 is deducted in the bridge from EBITDA of 107,581 to Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165, together with 4,059 of acquisition costs and 4,405 of stock compensation (S7 page:7), but it remains inside reported operating income of 77,451 and net income of 47,264. Q3 2025 shows the opposite: a 23,300 earn-out charge depressed reported operating income of 10,087 (S4 page:4). Comparing Q3 2026 with Q3 2025 reported earnings therefore overstates the underlying change; Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165 against 47,351 is the cleaner comparison but is still a management figure and still mixes perimeters (PAG contributed 173,666 of Q3 2026 revenue, S4 page:30). The retained quarters tie: Q1 55,430 plus Q2 86,024 equals H1 2026 of 141,454 (S6 page:7), and H1 plus Q3 107,165 equals the 9M 2026 figure of 248,619.

Cash conversion is the weak spot. Operating cash flow was 21,284 for 9M 2026 after inventory rose 148,409 in the cash flow statement (S4 page:6), while balance-sheet inventory rose from 553,834 to 893,006, which includes 200,179 of inventory acquired with PAG (S4 page:10). Free cash flow was negative 3,415 for 9M 2026 and positive 46,619 in Q3 2026 (S7 page:7); the Q3 figure alone cannot be annualised. Management expects "strong fourth quarter free cash flow" (S7 page:2), a forward statement the filings do not evidence.
### Consistency with the CP-0 handoff

The CP-0 handoff said the filed statements cover every needed period, the credit agreement and first amendment are missing, 2026 cash interest is missing and the net-debt definition in the releases deducts issuance costs. This handoff confirms each against the pages cited and corrects nothing in CP-0. It adds one detail CP-0 left open: unused revolver commitments are printed for every quarter-end (S1 page:33, S2 page:23, S3 page:29, S4 page:32), so liquidity by period is supplied.

This handoff sets out the business, ownership, transaction and governance context for VSE CORP (registrant VSE Corporation, ticker VSEC, issuer id vsec) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, cutoff 2026-11-05. Its reader question is which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor. Each fact row is tagged Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Figures are USD.
## Sources

S1 to S4 are filed documents and control; S5 to S7 are management releases and appear as Management Language or as attributed support. Pages were read at the locators cited, not the whole of every source. No external source is used.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| VSE is a listed aviation aftermarket distributor and repairer that changed shape in 2026 through the PAG purchase, funded mainly by equity and a new term loan. Customer concentration, OEM dependence and integration are the business risks. | Medium | The purchase agreement, credit agreement and seller exchange documents are not in the pack, and the headline and accounting prices for PAG differ with no stated bridge. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The PAG acquisition closed on 2026-05-05 at about USD 2.02 billion of accounting consideration and repair rose to 58.8% of Q3 2026 revenue from 37.8% a year earlier. | Scale and engine repair content support margins, but integration, preliminary purchase accounting and leverage now sit together. | Medium |

| Funding was mainly equity, about USD 1.3 billion net of offering proceeds, plus a USD 900.0 million term loan B; no sponsor or controlling holder is named. | Equity limited the debt added, but no sponsor exists to supply or withhold support; beneficial ownership is outside the pack. | Medium |

| About one fifth of FY2025 revenue came from one affiliated customer group, and engine repair rests on OEM licenses and repair approvals. | Loss of that group or an OEM license would hit revenue and margin; concentration after the acquisition is not disclosed. | Medium |

| The PAG seller holds exchangeable shares under lock-up and registration rights, and an earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million may be paid in cash or equity at VSE's option. | A share overhang and a possible cash call after 2026 results are open; the governing agreements are not supplied. | Medium |

| The PAG headline price of USD 2.025 billion and the accounting consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand differ, and the sources give no bridge. | Transaction size must be quoted with its basis; the difference cannot be reconciled from the pack. | High |
### Business and transaction view

VSE is a single-segment aviation aftermarket business that sells parts (distribution) and repairs components and engines (repair), and in 2026 it bought its way into a larger engine-repair and distribution platform. The strongest support for a creditor is that the largest deal, Precision Aviation Group (PAG), was funded with a large equity raise and tangible equity units alongside a USD 900.0 million term loan B, that PAG already contributes about a third of quarterly revenue, and that the group has raised equity repeatedly since 2024 to fund acquisitions. The weakest points are concentration (one affiliated customer group at about 20% of FY2025 revenue), dependence on OEM licenses and approvals for the highest-value repairs, and an acquisition pace that leaves purchase accounting preliminary for several deals at once. What decides the outcome is integration of PAG and the Q4 2026 cash flow, because debt now rests mostly on floating-rate bank facilities, and because the documents that govern control rights (credit agreement, purchase agreement amendment, exchange and registration agreements) are not in the pack. Management's characterisations (record results, leading position, sole-source repairs) are quoted as Management Language below and are not adopted.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence and locator | Credit relevance |

| Core activities | Aftermarket parts distribution and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) for aircraft components, engine accessories and, after 2026, engine components and avionics | Documentary Fact | S1 page:4 "The Aviation segment is a leading provider of aftermarket parts distribution and MRO services"; S4 page:21 | Aftermarket demand follows flight hours and fleet age, not new aircraft deliveries, supporting revenue durability but exposed to air travel downturns (S1 page:9) |

| Segments | One reportable segment, Aviation, after the Fleet and Federal and Defense sales | Documentary Fact | S4 page:21 "manages its business as a single reportable and operating segment" | No segment margin disclosure; mix shifts between repair and distribution are visible only through revenue by type |

| Revenue streams | Q3 2026 revenue 541,006 USD k: repair 318,024 (58.8%), distribution 222,982; Q3 2025 repair was 106,874 of 282,909 (37.8%) | Documentary Fact | S4 page:16 and page:17 | Repair carries OEM approvals and labor intensity; the mix shift follows acquisitions (PAG contributed 173,666 of Q3 revenue, S4 page:11, and 173.7 million in S4 page:30, but PAG's own repair and distribution split is Not supplied) |

| End markets and customers | Commercial airlines, regional airlines, cargo, MRO providers, manufacturers, corporate owners and fixed-base operators; Q3 2026 revenue 535,080 commercial and 5,926 government | Documentary Fact | S1 page:4; S4 page:16 | Government is about 1.1% of Q3 revenue, so defense budget risk is small; commercial cycle risk dominates |

| Customer concentration | One group of affiliated customers under common ownership was 20% of FY2025 revenue, 21% for FY2024 and 14% for FY2023 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:11 "collectively accounted for approximately 20% of the Company"; S1 page:70 | Single-name concentration is the main revenue-durability risk; the 2026 10-Qs give no update after PAG, so current exposure is Not supplied |

| Geography | FY2025 revenue by billing address: United States 629,665, Canada 149,034, other countries 333,576 (USD k) | Documentary Fact | S1 page:70 | Foreign revenue (about 43% of FY2025, calculated below) exposes VSE to export controls and trade policy (S1 page:10) |

| OEM relationships and licenses | Exclusive license to manufacture, sell, market, distribute and repair certain Pratt & Whitney PT6 fuel pumps (USD 10.8 million, 16-year intangible life); Atech repairs support Pratt & Whitney Canada platforms | Documentary Fact | S4 page:14 "exclusively manufacture, sell, market, distribute, and repair certain fuel pumps for use on the Pratt & Whitney PT6 engine series"; S4 page:15; S7 page:2 | Licensed content gives pricing power but ties margin to OEM goodwill; license terms and termination rights are Not supplied |

| Management characterisation | Atech has repair approvals covering more than 300 part numbers, "including sole-source repairs for flight-critical components"; organic growth about 17% | Management Language | S7 page:2 | Promotional; not verified by a filed statement; treat as attributed |

| Pricing and volume drivers | Revenue growth credited to acquisitions, newly awarded OEM distribution agreements and sustained demand | Documentary Fact | S4 page:30 | Pricing mechanics and contract tenor are Not supplied: no contract terms or backlog figure in the pack |

| Cost structure | Q3 2026 cost of products 177,921 against product revenue 222,982 and cost of services 266,138 against service revenue 318,024 (USD k); intangible amortization 23,095 shown separately | Documentary Fact | S4 page:4 | Cost-of-sales margins of about 20.2% on products and 16.3% on services (calculated below) before selling, general and administrative and amortization |

| Capital spending | Purchases of property and equipment 24,699 for 9M 2026 and 21,281 for FY2025 (USD k) | Documentary Fact | S4 page:6; S1 page:43 | Capital intensity is low (about 1.9% of 9M 2026 revenue), so cash conversion depends on working capital |

| Working capital | Inventories 893,006 at 2026-09-30 against 553,834 at 2025-12-31; the cash flow statement shows a 148,409 inventory build for 9M 2026 "in support of a new OEM auxiliary power unit program and engine initiatives" | Documentary Fact | S4 page:4; S4 page:6; S4 page:33 | Inventory is about 19.9% of total assets (calculated below); a stalled program or slow-moving stock would strain cash and the inventory valuation the auditor flagged (S1 page:39) |

| Regulation | Repairs may be performed only at certified facilities with certified technicians; FAA certification is required before installation | Documentary Fact | S1 page:8 | Certification is a barrier to entry and a single-point risk if a facility loses approval |
### Company profile
| Field | Value | Category | Source |
| Legal name and form | VSE Corporation, Delaware, incorporated 1959 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:1; S1 page:3 |
| Listing | Common stock VSEC and 5.750% tangible equity units VSECU, NASDAQ Global Select Market; large accelerated filer | Documentary Fact | S4 page:1 |
| Headquarters and country | Miramar, Florida, United States | Documentary Fact | S4 page:1 |
| Sector | Services-Engineering Services (context setting, not issuer evidence) | Documentary Fact | Run context |
| Business description | Aftermarket parts distribution and MRO for air transportation assets, commercial and government | Documentary Fact | S1 page:3 |
| Employees | Approximately 1,600 at 2025-12-31, before PAG; current headcount Not supplied | Documentary Fact | S1 page:5 |
| Shares outstanding | 28,071,358 common shares at 2026-10-30; 9,200,000 tangible equity units issued in February 2026 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:1; S4 page:26 |
| Holders | About 185 stockholders of record at 2026-02-20; beneficial ownership is in the proxy statement, which is not in the pack | Insufficient Information | S1 page:26; S1 page:79 |
| Sponsor, parent, guarantors | None named in the context or the filings; subsidiary guarantors are mentioned only generically | Insufficient Information | S1 page:81 |
| Auditor | Grant Thornton LLP, auditor since 2019; FY2025 opinion unmodified in form ("present fairly, in all material respects") | Documentary Fact | S1 page:41; S1 page:39 |
| Fiscal year | Year ending December 31 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:1 |
| Ratings | Not supplied (context blank, not zero) | Insufficient Information | Run context |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction that defines the period is the acquisition of Precision Aviation Group (PAG), a portfolio company of GenNx360 Capital Partners, under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2026-01-29 and completed on 2026-05-05. Status: completed. The parties named in the executed agreement listing are VSE Corporation, two VSE acquisition vehicles, GenNx/PAG IntermediateCo Inc. and GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC (S1 page:79); a first amendment to the agreement dated 2026-05-04, an exchange and redemption agreement, a registration rights agreement and two lock-up agreements, all dated 2026-05-05 and all with GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC, are listed as exhibits (S3 page:33), but none of those documents is in the pack, so their terms are Insufficient Information. The second-quarter 10-Q summarises the deal as total consideration of "approximately $2.02 billion" (S3 page:9). The 10-K and the first-quarter 10-Q describe total upfront consideration of approximately USD 2.025 billion, in the Q1 10-Q "consisting of $1.750 billion in cash" plus an in-kind payment of 1,415,752 shares of newly issued equity of a VSE subsidiary, with up to USD 125.0 million of contingent earn-out on PAG's 2026 adjusted EBITDA (S1 page:73; S2 page:20). The later 10-Qs record total purchase consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand: cash paid 1,770,370, less cash acquired 22,215, equity at fair value 238,002 and an earn-out at acquisition-date fair value of 33,850 (S3 page:9; S4 page:9 and page:10). These are two bases for the same deal and are logged as a conflict below, not reconciled.

Use of proceeds and sources. The cash price was funded by a February 2026 common stock offering of 4,587,766 shares at USD 188.00 per share (net proceeds USD 829.0 million) and a tangible equity unit offering of 9,200,000 units at a stated USD 50.00 each (net proceeds USD 444.9 million), together about USD 1.3 billion net, plus borrowings of USD 900.0 million under a new term loan B (S4 page:26 and page:29; S2 page:20). Each unit combines a prepaid stock purchase contract, settled in shares on 2029-02-01 within a range of 0.2171 to 0.2660 shares per contract, and a senior unsecured amortizing note paying 5.93% per annum with final installment on 2029-02-01 (S4 page:19, page:26 and page:27). The new debt issues are therefore the term loan B (USD 900.0 million, due 2033-05-05, status: funded 2026-05-05, USD 897.75 million outstanding at 2026-09-30), the revolver upsize from USD 400.0 million to USD 500.0 million (due 2030-05-02, USD 20.0 million drawn at 2026-09-30) and the amortizing notes (USD 61.043 million outstanding at 2026-09-30); the prior term loan was repaid in full, and a debt commitment letter whose bridge and backstop commitments "were reduced to $0" had been signed with the purchase agreement (S4 page:18; S1 page:29). Debt issuance costs of USD 20.8 million were incurred on the amendment (S4 page:18). Liquidity effect and leverage after the deal are in the prior handoff (CP-1): principal debt of USD 978.8 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 296.3 million at 2025-12-31.

Other transactions. Atech Turbine Components, acquired on 2026-08-31 for USD 64.1 million net of cash acquired and funded with cash and revolver borrowings; NorthStar Technologies, acquired on 2026-04-01 for USD 10.1 million; Aero 3, acquired on 2025-12-23 for USD 346.1 million as revised (S2 stated 346.4); each is described as not material or preliminary (S4 page:9, page:12 and page:13). Subsequent event: Test Logic, Inc. was acquired on 2026-10-05, funded with cash on hand, price not disclosed (S4 page:27). Transaction-related status risks: the PAG, Atech, NorthStar and Aero 3 purchase price allocations are preliminary (S4 page:9 to page:15).

Ownership and control. VSE is a public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder named in the filings or the context; beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information. After closing, the PAG seller holds 1,415,752 shares of a VSE subsidiary, exchangeable at any time and automatically exchanged into Company common stock on a one-for-one basis if not exchanged by 2029-05-05, "subject to a lock-up period" whose length is not stated (S4 page:10). That makes the seller a potential holder of a significant block once exchanged; its percentage of common stock is not stated and is not inferred here.
### Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour

spans.text: ## Request

This handoff gives the fundamental credit view of VSE CORP (VSE Corporation, ticker VSEC) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway, in USD, for Q3 2026 against FY2025. It synthesises the earlier source-readiness, financial-base and business-and-transaction work into a credit assessment, strengths and weaknesses, key findings, key risks and gaps. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

Issuer sources behind the upstream figures, with the labels used below. Locators are `page:N`, the chunk of the converted file, not the printed page. Figures in this handoff come from the upstream handoffs and were rechecked against these pages where cited.

| S7 | EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl | 433c5d4af4ceef97f7133d6bf32c06676acee7a23adece5c52f374d8108500f0 |

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| VSE is a profitable but newly stretched aviation aftermarket credit: net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA after a large acquisition, liquidity is adequate, and the outcome hinges on integration and year-end cash flow. | Medium | Covenant levels, the credit agreement and 2026 cash interest are missing, so headroom and cash interest cover cannot be measured; acquisition-adjusted earnings are management's figure. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt rose to 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA from 1.24x at December 2025; management guidance implies about 2.6x at year-end even if net debt does not fall. | Leverage should ease as acquired earnings annualise, but that rests on guidance, not filed results. | Medium |

| Liquidity of USD 545.0 million covers the USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months many times; the revolver matures in 2030 and the term loan in 2033. | Near-term refinancing risk is low. | High |

| Free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million for nine months after a large inventory build, though the third quarter produced USD 46.6 million. | Deleveraging leans on a strong fourth quarter that is a management expectation; inventory-heavy growth ties up cash. | Medium |

| About USD 667.8 million of floating-rate secured debt is unhedged, so each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest. | Interest cost is rate-sensitive, though trailing adjusted EBITDA covers contractual interest 5.20x at current rates. | Medium |

| One customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue, OEM licenses support repair margins, and goodwill and intangibles are 62.6% of assets. | Loss of the group or an OEM approval would hit earnings, and acquired intangibles give little tangible asset support. | Medium |
### Credit view

VSE Corporation is a profitable aviation aftermarket credit that has become much larger and materially more leveraged, and its credit quality now depends on integrating the Precision Aviation Group business and turning earnings into cash. The strongest support is earnings growth, with a record Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.8% in Q3 2026, liquidity of USD 545.0 million and annual scheduled principal of no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031. The weakest point is cash conversion: free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million for the nine months to September 2026 while net debt stands at 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA and the covenant levels are unknown. Delivery of the fourth-quarter cash flow management expects, with margins holding, decides the outcome.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Adequate and improving but newly leveraged: leverage is above the 2025 level, liquidity and maturity profile are comfortable, and cash conversion and covenant headroom are unproven | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity, maturity and cash flow figures; CP-1A concentration, funding mix and integration rows |

| Thesis | VSE's strong aftermarket earnings and equity-funded acquisition financing support its debt, provided the integration of the acquired business converts earnings into free cash flow before leverage-sensitive covenants and floating rates bite | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |

| Why confidence is not High | CP-1A judges this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; the credit agreement is not supplied; acquisition-adjusted earnings have no schedule; 2026 cash interest is missing | Insufficient Information | Medium | CP-0 gaps; CP-1 gaps; CP-1A gaps |
### Financial risk and liquidity
| Measure | Value | Period and basis | Category | Source |
| Principal debt | USD 978.8 million, of which 93.8% is secured bank debt | 2026-09-30; term loan B 897.75, revolver 20.0, unsecured amortizing notes 61.043 (USD m) | Documentary Fact | S4 page:17 |
| Total debt / TTM Adjusted EBITDA | 3.26x | 2026-09-30; management TTM Adjusted EBITDA USD 300.4 million | Documentary Fact (calculated in CP-1) | S7 page:7 |

| Net debt / TTM Adjusted EBITDA | 3.04x; 2.35x on management's acquisition-adjusted earnings of USD 389.2 million | 2026-09-30; net debt is principal less cash, USD 913.0 million | Documentary Fact; Management Language for the 2.35x basis | S7 page:7 |
| Net debt / TTM Adjusted EBITDA, prior | 1.24x | 2025-12-31 | Documentary Fact | S7 page:7 |

| TTM Adjusted EBITDA / contractual annual interest | 5.20x (6.74x on acquisition-adjusted earnings) | Contractual interest USD 57.7 million at 2026-09-30 rates, before swaps and fees | Analyst Interpretation | S4 page:17; S4 page:19 |
| Liquidity | USD 545.0 million: cash USD 65.8 million plus USD 479.2 million unused revolver | 2026-09-30 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:4; S4 page:32 |
| Principal due within twelve months | USD 32.3 million (current portion of long-term debt) | 2026-09-30 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:4 |
| Free cash flow | Negative USD 3.4 million for nine months; USD 46.6 million for Q3 2026 | Management definition, operating cash flow less capital expenditures | Documentary Fact | S7 page:7 |
| Interest-rate exposure | USD 917.75 million floating secured debt less USD 250.0 million of swaps leaves USD 667.8 million unhedged | 2026-09-30 | Analyst Interpretation | S4 page:17; S4 page:19 |
### Key findings

1. VSE has levered up through an equity-heavy acquisition, and its leverage path is mostly a matter of earnings timing. Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA against 1.24x at December 2025 [CP-1 leverage chart; S7 page:7], because the trailing earnings include only five months of the acquired business while all of its debt is on the balance sheet. Management's full-year 2026 guidance of revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.9% to 19.1% [S7 page:3] implies full-year Adjusted EBITDA of about USD 347 million to USD 354 million (calculated below), which would put net debt at about 2.6x on a flat net debt. This is a mechanical, not a proven, deleveraging, and it relies on guidance that the filings do not yet evidence (Analyst Interpretation on a Management Language basis). The credit implication is that leverage tolerance is acceptable if the guided run-rate is delivered and thin if the acquired earnings disappoint.

2. VSE's liquidity and maturity profile make near-term default or refinancing risk low. Cash of USD 65.8 million and unused revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million total USD 545.0 million against USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months, and annual scheduled principal is no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031, with the balance of the term loan due from 2032, mostly at its 2033 maturity [CP-1 maturity wall; S4 page:19]. The risk mechanic that remains is acquisition spending: the revolver helps fund bolt-on deals (Atech, acquired on 2026-08-31, was funded with cash and revolver borrowings, and USD 20.0 million was drawn at 2026-09-30 [S4 page:9 and page:17]) so liquidity can fall if acquisitions continue before free cash flow turns up.

3. Cash conversion is the weak spot. Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months and free cash flow negative USD 3.4 million, after a USD 148.4 million inventory build [CP-1; S4 page:6], while Q3 2026 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million. Growth programs, including the new OEM auxiliary power unit program the Company names [S4 page:33], absorb inventory ahead of revenue. The credit implication is that debt reduction comes from year-end working capital release and earnings, not from structural cash generation shown so far; the write-down of slow-moving inventories was a critical audit matter in FY2025 [S1 page:40].

4. VSE's cost of debt is floating and only partly hedged. Secured floating debt is USD 917.75 million with USD 250.0 million of swaps, leaving about USD 667.8 million exposed; each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest, about 2.2% of trailing adjusted EBITDA (calculated below). Trailing adjusted EBITDA covers contractual annual interest of USD 57.7 million 5.20x. Cash interest cover cannot be shown for 2026 because cash interest is not reported (FY2025 was 6.81x) [CP-1].

5. The business risks are concentration and dependence on OEMs. One affiliated customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and its post-acquisition share is not disclosed [CP-1A; S1 page:11]; repair, now 58.8% of Q3 2026 revenue, depends on OEM approvals and licenses such as the Pratt & Whitney PT6 fuel pump license [CP-1A; S4 page:14]. The mechanism is that the loss of the group or an approval removes high-margin work while inventory and capacity remain. The implication is that earnings quality is exposed to two single points of failure whose terms are not in the pack.

6. Creditor control and structure cannot be tested. The filings say a maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio exist and were met [S4 page:19], but give no levels; the credit agreement, its first amendment and the seller's exchange and registration agreements are not supplied. Management's own leverage measures use different definitions. The implication is that headroom, permitted distributions and the effect of a possible share overhang on equity market access (used four times since 2024 to fund acquisitions) are open.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Earnings scale and margin (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the characterisations). VSE's Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 107.2 million in Q3 2026 at a margin of 19.8% against 16.7% a year earlier, and in Q3 2026 adjustments net to a small deduction (EBITDA of USD 107.6 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 107.2 million [S7 page:7]), so that margin is close to unadjusted; over nine months add-backs are about a tenth of adjusted EBITDA. Basis: CP-1 financials and credit metrics; CP-1A cost-of-sales margin rows. The mechanism is operating leverage from a repair-weighted mix, which supports debt service if sustained.

Equity-funded acquisition financing (Documentary Fact). About USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the PAG purchase, and unit holders' prepaid stock purchase contracts settle in shares in 2029, so the equity layer under the debt grew and the units add only USD 61.0 million of debt. Basis: CP-1A transaction summary; CP-1 debt table. This lowers debt-to-capitalisation (book debt about 24.7% of book debt plus equity, calculated below).

Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 545.0 million of liquidity, a revolver to 2030, and a term loan to 2033 with USD 9.0 million a year of amortization leave no large refinancing event until 2030, and then only the USD 20.0 million revolver draw. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts.

Diversified end markets with a repair moat (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is 98.9% commercial across airlines, cargo, MRO providers and owners, and FAA-certified repair capacity and OEM licenses are barriers to entry. Basis: CP-1A company and operating model rows. The mechanism is aftermarket demand tied to fleet usage rather than new deliveries.
Weaknesses.

Cash conversion (Documentary Fact). Nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million after a USD 148.4 million inventory build, with inventories at about 19.9% of total assets. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A working capital row. A stalled OEM program would raise net debt while earnings look stable.

Leverage and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA, with about USD 667.8 million of unhedged floating debt. Basis: CP-1 leverage and liquidity figures. Rising rates or an earnings miss would compress cover; covenant levels are unknown.
Customer and OEM concentration (Documentary Fact). A single customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and PAG's customer mix is not disclosed. Basis: CP-1A concentration row.

Acquired-asset and integration risk (Documentary Fact). Goodwill and intangibles are 62.6% of total assets, tangible equity is only USD 178.7 million, purchase accounting is preliminary for several deals, and internal controls are being integrated. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A integration row. This limits balance-sheet support in a stress and increases impairment risk if acquired earnings disappoint; it is a mechanic, not a recovery view.

Opaque creditor protections (Insufficient Information). Covenant levels, guarantor and security details, and seller-agreement terms are Not supplied, which matters for headroom, structural position and distributions.
### Key credit risks

| Integration and earnings delivery on the acquired business | Management guidance and the trailing-earnings annualisation assume the acquired business holds margin; a miss leaves full acquisition debt on lower earnings | Leverage stays near 3x or higher and deleveraging slips | Material |
